subject: NovaHealth inference eval kit + function-call / JSON schema playbook
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@novahealth.com>, Jake Lin <jake.lin@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: inference fit, benchmarks, JSON-schema & function-call plan

Hi Emily / Jake —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum on the NovaHealth pilot:

1) Objective and constraints
- Primary goal: structured extraction from clinical discharge summaries into your EHR ingest schema (patient_id, encounter_id, diagnosis_codes[], medication_list[], discharge_instructions.fragments).
- Latency SLO: target 450ms median per request; burst tolerance up to 1s.
- Data handling: PHI in payloads; you requested encryption-in-flight + customer-managed KMS for keys.

2) Recommended model & why
- Baseline suggestion: rw-13b-opt-q8 (8-bit weight-quantized 13B) for best balance of quality on long clinical context and cost.
- Fallback: rw-7b-fast (lower cost, sharper tail-latency) for burst routing or non-critical backfill.
- Notes: we plan to run a 48-hour head-to-head on your prompt set to validate entity recall/precision vs sample annotator labels.

3) Evaluation artifacts we shared (attached + links)
- novahealth_eval_promptset_v1.jsonl (prompt/response pairs derived from 200 de-identified records)
- benchmark_summary_apr15.pdf (initial latency / token-cost projections)
- schema_contract_v2.docx (proposed JSON schema for EHR ingest + required validation rules)
- HubSpot record and Drive folder: see links below.

4) Function-calling & JSON schema compliance concerns
- We recommend testing two modes: (A) structured output (model outputs JSON that is validated against your schema), and (B) function-calling where the model returns a function invocation payload that we execute server-side.
- Key tests we want to run in the pilot:
  * JSON schema strictness: must fail fast on schema mismatch, and we should measure failure rate and types (missing fields vs bad types).
  * Retry behavior: define idempotency for each retry attempt (we should not double-insert into EHR). We'll scope a retry policy (max 2 retries, exponential backoff) and a replay-safe wrapper on ingestion.
  * Tool call reliability: assert that when the model emits function calls, the serialized args strictly conform to the schema. Include a fuzz suite for malformed args.

5) Proposed next steps (timeline)
- Today: I shared the eval kit and schema (attachments + Drive).
- By EOD Thu (Apr 15): NovaHealth team to confirm consent to run the 48-hour head-to-head on the provided prompt set and confirm KMS approach.
- Mon Apr 19: Redwood to deliver a small-run benchmark (1000 records) with both models and provide evaluation metrics (precision/recall on core entities, JSON schema failure types, median latency).
- Tue Apr 20: follow-up call to review results and discuss contract path / Dedicated capacity sizing.

Please reply with any immediate questions or if you want us to adjust the schema contract before the run.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: novahealth_eval_promptset_v1.jsonl (jsonl), schema_contract_v2.docx (docx), benchmark_summary_apr15.pdf (pdf)
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@novahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jake Lin <jake.lin@novahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-15T12:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference fit, benchmarks, JSON-schema & function-call plan

Thanks Vanessa — great summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency SLO: 450ms median is aggressive for our existing pipeline; can you confirm expected p50/p95 on the rw-13b-opt-q8 with a 4k token context? If p95 spikes above 1.2s we may need to consider a dedicated pool.

2) Security/KMS: procurement looped in procurement@novahealth.com — we need a diagram of the key lifecycle and whether Redwood can support our HSM-backed KMS (we can share an architecture contact).

3) Function calls & retries: we like the retry safety notes. For the pilot, can you provide a deterministic way to detect duplicate ingestion attempts (suggested: include a request_id and model_invocation_id in the function call payload)? Also: we need to ensure function-call arg types match exactly — even small schema diffs will break our parser.

We confirm we’re OK for Redwood to run the 48-hour head-to-head on the provided prompt set pending procurement signoff. Can you also include an example of a malformed function-call response and how Redwood’s runtime would surface it in the console?

—Emily
Emily Ross
Director, Clinical Data Integration, NovaHealth
emily.ross@novahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@novahealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference fit, benchmarks, JSON-schema & function-call plan

Emily — quick technical plan to address your items (copying Aditya for infra/KMS notes):

1) Expected latency (rw-13b-opt-q8)
- Internal micro-benchmarks with 4k context: p50 ~ 300-380ms, p95 ~ 920-1,050ms on NVLink-cluster g4p-equivalent. We will run an identical 1000-record sample to confirm.

2) KMS / HSM support
- We support customer-provided KMS keys via our Private deployment flow and can integrate to an HSM-backed key provider. Aditya to draft the key-diagram and required controls (will attach the KMS integration checklist).

3) Function-call validation & retry plan
- Payload design: each request will include request_id (UUID), record_id (your EHR id), and attempt_number. Function invocation payload example: 

  {
    "request_id": "uuid-...",
    "record_id": "NH-ENC-12345",
    "model_invocation_id": "inv-20270416-xyz",
    "payload": { ... }
  }

- Duplicate detection: our ingestion shim will store model_invocation_id and only apply state transitions if not seen. We'll provide a read-only audit log keyed by model_invocation_id.
- Malformed response handling: runtime will attempt JSON schema validation; on failure it returns a structured error object into the console and pushes the full payload (with masked PHI) to the error bucket. Sample console error (will be included in the runbook):

  [ERROR] JSON-SCHEMA-MISMATCH: missing required field 'patient_id' (message_id inv-20270416-abc)

4) Test harness & checklist (what we will run during the 48-hour)
- Head-to-head: rw-13b-opt-q8 vs rw-7b-fast, 1k record batch each (same seed).
- Metrics: entity-level precision/recall, schema-failure-rate, median latency, retry count distribution, token-cost.
- Function-call tests: 200 invocations with intentional fuzz (type errors, missing fields, extra fields) to verify detection & retry path.

I attached a compact test plan to the Drive link. We'll also include a small sample of intentionally malformed function-call payloads so you can validate our error surfacing.

Marissa Cole
Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
